title: 4063. Longest Subarray Divisible by K with At Most One Negation I

examples.explanation: The sum of the entire array is 7, and 7 % 3 = 1, so it is not divisible by k = 3. Negating nums[2] = 2 changes the sum to 4 + 1 − 2 = 3, which is divisible by k. Therefore, the entire array is a valid subarray, giving a length of 3.

The sum of the entire array is 12, and negating any one of its elements does not make its sum divisible by 7. However, the subarray [3, 4] has a sum of 7, which is divisible by k = 7 without any negation. Therefore, the longest valid subarray has a length of 2.

The sum of the entire array is 9, and negating any one of its elements does not make its sum divisible by 6. The subarray [2, 2] has a sum of 4. Negating either element changes it to [-2, 2] or [2, -2], both of which have a sum of 0. Therefore, the longest valid subarray has a length of 2.
